questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include the name and description of the materials; health hazards; fire or explosion risks; steps to take in an accident; how to handle fires; how to handle spills or leaks; and first aid measures.

questions.question: What happens to a distracted driver?

options.text: Is usually aware of what is happening around them.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually perceives things more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower perception, delayed decisions, and wrong actions. Watch for distracted drivers and stay away from them when you can.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead.
questions.explanation: When someone tailgates you, add more space in front of your vehicle. This makes it easier for them to pass. Speeding up is not helpful because they may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how much liquid should be loaded into a tank?

options.text: How much the liquid will expand

questions.correctAnswerText: The color of the liquid
questions.explanation: The amount of liquid to load depends on how much it will expand during transport, its weight, and legal weight limits. Color does not affect safe loading.

questions.question: What should you check before driving in winter?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your heating and defrosting systems, coolant and antifreeze, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, reflectors, and exhaust system. Clear ice and snow from all windows, mirrors, steps, and radiator shutters.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave open space on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side.
questions.explanation: When turning right, avoid swinging too wide to the left. Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb. Leaving space on your right side tells other drivers you might be turning left, so they may try to pass you on the right.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Rims with a missing lug nut are okay if at least four other lug nuts remain.
A cracked lock ring is safe if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
Welded repairs are safe for rear axle wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous defects. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are not safe. Wheels or rims with welded repairs are not safe.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles transporting hazardous materials.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often use curved convex mirrors. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: How does doubling your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph affect braking distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase braking distance. When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance multiplies by four.

questions.question: How much water does a road need for hydroplaning to happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle's tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water. It does not take much water on the road for this to occur.

questions.question: If shipping papers show "Inhalation Hazard", what must you do?

options.text: Use an inhalation hazard placard only if you are carrying more than 100 pounds.
Always use an inhalation hazard placard.
You do not need an inhalation hazard placard for trips within your state.
Use an inhalation hazard placard only if you are crossing state lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use an inhalation hazard placard.
questions.explanation: If shipping papers show "Inhalation Hazard", you must use the proper inhalation hazard placard plus any other required placards. This rule applies no matter how much material you are carrying.

questions.question: Where should you keep shipping papers?

options.text: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or another easy-to-reach spot while wearing your seat belt. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When filling a tank divided by bulkheads, which sections should hold the most?

options.text: The section closest to the front.
The section closest to the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle sections.
questions.explanation: Fill tank sections evenly to distribute weight properly. Do not put too much weight in the front or rear sections.

questions.question: How can you most easily spot a trailer skid?

options.text: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer is still in its lane.
Release and then push the brake pedal again.
Watch for a jackknife warning light on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer is still in its lane.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors anytime you brake hard. Your mirrors will show if your trailer is still in the right position.

questions.question: Low clearance trailers are difficult to drive in which situation?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are difficult for low clearance trailers. This is especially true for low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers.

questions.question: If a trailer jackknifes, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes to let the wheels regain traction. Do not use the trailer hand brake because it will make the skid worse. Braking is what locked the wheels in the first place.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Turn back to straighten the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate.
questions.explanation: To fix a drive-wheel braking skid, lift your foot off the brake so the wheels can roll again. Turn quickly in the direction you want to go, then turn back to prevent skidding the other way.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that is black because of road debris.
Ice that is easy to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like wet pavement rather than ice.

questions.question: When driving slower than 40 mph, how many seconds of distance should you keep for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One second.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, keep one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: How do you test hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times, then press hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times, then press hard for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move down.
Pump the brakes three times, then press hard for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump the brakes three times, then press hard for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times, then press hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To test hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then press hard and hold for five seconds. The pedal should stay in place. If it moves, there may be a leak.
